newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin spokesman cautious on U.S.-Russia talks.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin spokesman cautious on U.S.-Russia talks.

text.p: Russia and the United States failed to reach a breakthrough on the thorny issue of NATO's eastwards expansion after talks with visiting U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, the Kremlin spokesman said on Friday.
"It's premature to talk about a breakthrough," Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing. "I would rather say one can express cautious optimism."

Albright met President Boris Yeltsin, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on Thursday and Friday to calm Moscow's fears about NATO plans to grant membership to some central and eastern European countries.

Yastrzhembsky said Russia, which remained opposed to expansion, sought a strong deal with NATO which would guarantee its security interests. "Russia will be satisfied only with a legally binding document," he said.
U.S. spokesman Nicholas Burns said earlier that Washington still believed the document should not be legally binding.
Yastrzhembsky made clear Moscow was not particularly impressed by the U.S. idea of forming a joint Russia-NATO brigade, to concentrate on peacekeeping issues.
"In the alphabet of our interests it is somwhere close to the first letter of my name," said Yastrzhembsky whose name starts with the last letter in the Russian alphabet.
But he indicated that Russia still hoped to work out a reasonable deal.
"Hard, intensive and uneasy work is under way on the document's contents," he said. "After all it does not matter what it is called. It is important that both parties are satisfied."
